subject: LinguaWorks pilot: success rubric, model choices, and localization fallback plan
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Hsu <lucy@linguaworks.ai>, Devin Patel <devin@linguaworks.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: LinguaWorks pilot: success rubric, model choices, and localization fallback plan

Hi Lucy / Devin —

Thanks again for a really helpful call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can get your pilot scheduled next week. I tried to keep this tightly action-oriented so we can turn it into the mutual action plan.

Summary of goal
- 6-week pilot to validate: 1) core English intent/response accuracy for customer support intents, 2) measured latency and per-token cost within your SLA targets, and 3) coverage for JP + ES fallback flows for top-10 intents.

Proposed success criteria (attached: POC-success-rubric.xlsx)
- Acceptance tests: macro accuracy >= 88% on curated test set of 1,200 utterances (weighted by volume).
- Latency: median response < 650ms at 1 qps steady-state; p95 < 1.2s.
- Cost: model-token cost <= $0.003/token on average across queries (we’ll run synthetic load to estimate).
- Safety/Hallucination: hallucination incidents < 1% (measured by seeded probes & manual spot checks).
- Ops: ability to roll back to fallback model automatically on degradation.

Model recommendations for the trial (attached: model-shortlist.csv)
- Primary: Mistral-Instruct-7B-v2 (best cost / quality balance for convo+RAG tasks).
- High-accuracy option: Llama-3-13B-chat (useful for edge cases in JP where translation quality is critical).
- Fallback: OPT-6.7B-quant (lower-cost, faster cold-start; used as automatic fallback under latency/cost thresholds).

Multilingual plan
- Core evaluation will focus on EN + JP + ES. For JP we propose a small parallel test set (200 utterances) and a translation-augmented eval to measure fidelity.
- Fallback routing: if model confidence < X or token cost spikes, route to fallback model with a deterministic translation post-process for JP/ES (we’ll provide pattern examples).

Operational milestones / timeline
- Week 0 (this week): sign off on mutual action plan + NDA addendum (if needed) + share sample dataset (anonymized).
- Week 1: environment access + baseline run with Mistral-Instruct-7B-v2 (functional validation).
- Week 2–3: focused eval (coverage & accuracy) + latency profiling and cost projection.
- Week 4: integration demo with your UI + live traffic shadowing.
- Week 5–6: acceptance window and tuning; go/no-go.

Roles / owners
- Redwood PM & lead: me (Stephanie) — overall pilot owner and first escalation.
- Customer success: Marissa Cole — onboarding & acceptance facilitation.
- Infra & model ops: Ben Carter — serves as engineering contact for model config, quantization, and routing policies.
- Customer tech lead: Devin — data ingestion and integration owner.

Immediate asks (for Monday kickoff)
1) Devin: share anonymized sample dataset (<= 5k rows) + example UI workflow screenshots.
2) Lucy: confirm the top-10 intents you want prioritized for JP/ES fallback.
3) Legal/procurement: let us know any minimal contract items (I’ve copied Ben & Marissa for handoff).

I’ve attached a concise rubric (POC-success-rubric.xlsx) and the initial model shortlist. If that looks good we’ll convert this into a mutual action plan and send a proposed kickoff calendar.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: LinguaWorks pilot: success rubric, model choices, and localization fallback plan

Hi Stephanie —

This looks great and really helpful — thanks for pulling it together. Quick answers inline:
- We can provide a 3k anonymized transcript sample by Monday (Devin will attach).
- Top-10 intents for JP/ES: ticket_create, ticket_status, billing_question, password_reset, agent_transfer, feedback_submit, subscription_cancel, promo_lookup, address_update, agent_feedback. I’ll send a CSV of intent priority.
- On the fallback approach: we like the idea of an automatic fallback to OPT-6.7B-quant if latency > 1s or cost > threshold.

One ask: our security team needs to see the data handling notes and whether KV cache is persisted outside the session. Could someone share a short note?

Cheers,
Lucy
Head of Product, LinguaWorks
lucy@linguaworks.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 12:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LinguaWorks pilot: success rubric, model choices, and localization fallback plan

Lucy —

Quick security/ops note: KV cache is kept in-memory per-session by default and not persisted to disk in our hosted flow. For private deployments we can configure strict in-VM memory-only policies and bring-your-own-KMS for keys. I’ll send the short security summary as a stub attachment (MVP-eval-scenarios.pdf) for your team.

On model ops: we recommend starting with Mistral-Instruct-7B-v2 at 8-bit quant (no latency regression expected) and a fallback flow to OPT-6.7B-quant. For JP edge cases we can enable Llama-3-13B-chat on a small canary if you see degradation.

I’ll provision a sandbox project and share API keys limited to the pilot once we get dataset access.

—
Ben Carter
